parameters.content:
## One lead, one decision record

The orchestrator owns sequence and nothing else. Qualification, every CRM write
and the outreach draft each live in their own service, so this workflow is a
readable list of steps rather than a place where logic hides.

A disqualified lead is never written to the CRM at all. A lead already in the
ledger is not re-qualified, so a retried webhook costs nothing and creates
nothing.

## Ingest key

The webhook is public, so the first thing it does is check an `x-swarm-key`
header against the `SWARM_INGEST_KEY` n8n variable.

If that variable is not set, every inbound lead is refused. An unset secret
reads as "refuse everything", never as "no secret required".

The Swarm Request trigger below is the internal entry point and skips this
check, because a caller is already inside n8n.

parameters.jsCode:
const raw = $input.first().json;
const r = (raw && raw.json) ? raw.json : raw;
const fx = $("Swarm Fixture Loop").first().json;
const crm = r.crm || {};
const out = r.outreach || {};
return [{ json: {
  case_id: fx.case_id,
  note: fx.note,
  expect_outcome: fx.expect_outcome,
  expect_tier: fx.expect_tier,
  expect_deal: fx.expect_deal,
  expect_outreach: fx.expect_outreach,
  expect_contact: fx.expect_contact,
  expect_tenant: fx.tenant_id,
  expect_trace: fx.trace_id,
  actual_outcome: r.outcome,
  actual_tier: (r.qualification || {}).tier || null,
  actual_score: (r.qualification || {}).score,
  actual_tenant: r.tenant_id,
  actual_trace: r.trace_id,
  rubric_version: ((r.qualification || {}).scoring || {}).rubric_version,
  has_contact: !!crm.contact_id,
  has_deal: !!crm.deal_id,
  has_task: !!crm.task_id,
  outreach_attempted: out.attempted === true,
  outreach_sent: out.sent === true,
  outreach_status: out.status || null,
  draft: String(out.draft || "").slice(0, 200),
  steps: (r.steps || []).length,
  latency_ms: r.latency_ms
} }];

parameters.content:
## End-to-end suite

Six leads through the whole swarm: qualification, CRM writes and outreach, all
in dry run. The tiers are fixed by supplying signals, so each case asserts
exactly which CRM objects should exist.

S02 re-sends S01. It must come back as a duplicate with nothing created, which
is the property that makes a retried webhook safe.

S06 supplies no signals and runs the real model end to end.

nodes.name: Build Callback
nodes.notes: Signs the completion with the per-execution callback_token from the dispatch payload. Hand-rolled SHA-256/HMAC because n8n Code nodes cannot rely on require("crypto"); verified against node:crypto by scripts/verify-callback-node.ts.

nodes.name: Callback Wanted?
nodes.notes: Only a run dispatched by the control plane has somewhere to report back to. A direct webhook post or a suite run skips the callback rather than inventing a destination.

nodes.name: Send Callback
nodes.notes: Delivers the signed completion. A failure here fails the execution on purpose: the control plane not learning the result is a real failure, and workflow 16 records it for replay.

description: Inbound lead to decision record. Deduplicates, qualifies through 12, writes contact, deal and the scoring rationale through 11, composes governed outreach through 13, and returns one auditable record of every step taken and every step skipped.
